title: at edit: a re-cite of a legacy row keeps the legacy reference, so the rewrite doctor asks for produces the blocking finding
body:
**No verb retires an acceptance test's legacy reference, and the one verb that looks like it does creates the blocking finding instead.** The doctor's advisory on a migrated row reads: `AT-01.1 carries a legacy reference and its thread is still Not Started -- it RESOLVES, nothing blocked; worth rewriting in the v3 grammar next time the thread is touched`. The rewrite it asks for is `intent at edit <ST> <AT> --file <path>` (or `--prose` for a non-test row). But `at_edit` builds the prospective row as `..existing.clone()` under its rule that a field you do not name is a field it does not change, so `legacy` is carried across the re-cite untouched, and the row now cites a test file AND carries a legacy reference, which `doctor` reports as `model-inconsistent`, blocking, exit 1: `these are alternatives, not a pair`. There is no `at rm`, and `at new` refuses a taken id, so a migrated row cannot be expressed in the v3 grammar at all. Surfaced by laksa-vc on Laksa, 2026-09-12: ST0093 AT-01.1 to AT-01.5 carry legacy refs to planned, unwritten test files, and hv wants the estate's `doctor -v` pristine.

**Ruled under the pen, 2026-09-12:** a re-cite that names `--file` or `--prose` IS the rewrite in the v3 grammar, so `at edit` retires `legacy` when either is named, and leaves it alone otherwise (a `--note` or `--covers` edit does not touch the citation). The `--kind` refusal in the same verb is the precedent: a verb must not create the disagreement `doctor` reports. One test, one arm: a legacy row re-cited with `--file` comes back with `file` set and `legacy` absent, and a `--note` edit of the same row leaves `legacy` in place. A red test row citing a planned, unwritten file is the normal to-write state and is not a finding.
